container_info.description:
The project aims to develop a **Commercial Energy Consumption Analytics & Anomaly Alerts** system that provides an intelligent monitoring layer for large commercial energy customers.

It uses interval meter data to surface consumption trends, benchmark against comparable sites, and generate alerts for significant deviations in usage.

This addresses the lack of customer-facing analytics and tools for account managers, helping reduce energy waste and improve customer retention.
container_info.reasoning: The container is explicitly a database container named PostgreSQLDatabase and the Dockerfile summary includes postgresql preinstalled. The project ingests interval meter time-series data and requires persistent, queryable storage for analytics and anomaly detection; PostgreSQL (optionally with time-series extensions) is the natural fit. The platform is therefore a database server rather than a web/mobile/backend framework.
requirements: initdb to initialize the database cluster
psql client for basic interactive queries and scripted setup
minimal configuration files (postgresql.conf and pg_hba.conf) with lightweight dev settings (listen_addresses, local trust for init, reduced logging)
single database and user creation script (CREATE ROLE / CREATE DATABASE) for automated agent setup
data directory with correct ownership/permissions (chown postgres) and a bind/mount point for persistence
environment variables for DB name, user, password, and port (PGDATABASE, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD, PGPORT) for headless operation
simple healthcheck script (psql -c 'SELECT 1') for container readiness
optional lightweight extension install step if required (e.g., timescaledb) but only if explicitly needed
minimal backup/restore tooling: pg_dump and pg_restore (only for basic validation)
no production monitoring, replication, or high-availability components included

steps.name: environment - persist DB env vars and verify CLIs
steps.description: Prepare workspace ownership, persist PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPORT to /etc/profile.d (world-readable for shells), and verify required Postgres CLIs are present. Do NOT persist PGPASSWORD. WORKSPACE may be injected via environment; scripts fall back to authoritative workspace path.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE:-/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/dt3_bootcamp_database/PostgreSQLDatabase}"
sudo mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) "$WORKSPACE"
: ${PGDATABASE:=devdb}
: ${PGUSER:=devuser}
: ${PGPORT:=5432}
# pick ephemeral port only if 5432 in use
if ss -ltn '( sport = :5432 )' | grep -q LISTEN; then PGPORT=$(shuf -i 20000-30000 -n1); fi
# persist minimal env; keep readable so non-root shells can source
sudo bash -c "cat > /etc/profile.d/pg_dev_env.sh <<EOF
export PGDATABASE='${PGDATABASE}'
export PGUSER='${PGUSER}'
export PGPORT='${PGPORT}'
EOF"
sudo chown root:root /etc/profile.d/pg_dev_env.sh && sudo chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/pg_dev_env.sh
# verify CLIs
command -v psql >/dev/null && command -v pg_dump >/dev/null && command -v pg_restore >/dev/null || { echo "Missing postgres CLIs" >&2; exit 2; }

steps.name: scaffolding - create workspace layout and helper scripts
steps.description: Create data, conf, and scripts directories in the workspace, create non-executable canonical SQL template for idempotent role/db creation, and create a robust healthcheck script that uses postgres superuser / pg_isready for readiness checks. Ensure data dir ownership is postgres for bind/mount persistence.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE:-/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/dt3_bootcamp_database/PostgreSQLDatabase}"
DATA_DIR="$WORKSPACE/data"; CONF_DIR="$WORKSPACE/conf"; SCRIPTS_DIR="$WORKSPACE/scripts"
sudo mkdir -p "$DATA_DIR" "$CONF_DIR" "$SCRIPTS_DIR" && sudo chown -R postgres:postgres "$DATA_DIR"
cat > "$SCRIPTS_DIR/create_dev_user_db.sql" <<'SQL'
-- idempotent template: creates role and database if missing
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = :'app_user') THEN
    EXECUTE format('CREATE ROLE %I WITH LOGIN PASSWORD %L', :'app_user', :'app_pass');
  END IF;
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = :'app_db') THEN
    EXECUTE format('CREATE DATABASE %I OWNER %I', :'app_db', :'app_user');
  END IF;
END$$;
SQL
chmod 644 "$SCRIPTS_DIR/create_dev_user_db.sql"
# healthcheck: prefer pg_isready then superuser psql (avoids app-user false negatives)
cat > "$SCRIPTS_DIR/healthcheck.sh" <<'BASH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE:-/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/dt3_bootcamp_database/PostgreSQLDatabase}"
: ${PGHOST:=127.0.0.1}; : ${PGPORT:=${PGPORT:-5432}}
pg_isready -h "$PGHOST" -p "$PGPORT" >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
# superuser check
sudo -u postgres psql -h "$PGHOST" -p "$PGPORT" -U postgres -c 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null
BASH
chmod 750 "$SCRIPTS_DIR/healthcheck.sh"

steps.name: configuration - initdb, write minimal confs, create idempotent SQL runner
steps.description: Initialize DB cluster in workspace data dir (as postgres), generate minimal postgresql.conf and pg_hba.conf using the persisted PGPORT (read from env or /etc/profile.d), create run_create_user_db.sh which executes SQL template as postgres user (trust auth) ensuring idempotent user/db creation. Validate port consistency between /etc/profile.d and postgresql.conf.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE:-/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/dt3_bootcamp_database/PostgreSQLDatabase}"
DATA_DIR="$WORKSPACE/data"; CONF_DIR="$WORKSPACE/conf"; SCRIPTS_DIR="$WORKSPACE/scripts"
# source persisted env if present
[ -f /etc/profile.d/pg_dev_env.sh ] && source /etc/profile.d/pg_dev_env.sh || true
: ${PGPORT:=5432}
# initdb if absent
sudo -u postgres bash -lc "[ -s '$DATA_DIR/PG_VERSION' ] || initdb -D '$DATA_DIR' --username=postgres --auth=trust >/dev/null"
# write postgresql.conf if missing and ensure it uses PGPORT
if [ ! -f "$CONF_DIR/postgresql.conf" ]; then
  sudo bash -lc "cat > '$CONF_DIR/postgresql.conf' <<EOF
listen_addresses = '*'
port = ${PGPORT}
logging_collector = off
log_min_messages = warning
shared_buffers = 32MB
max_connections = 50
EOF"
fi
# validate port consistency
conf_port=$(grep -E '^\s*port\s*=\s*' "$CONF_DIR/postgresql.conf" | sed -E 's/[^0-9]*([0-9]+).*/\1/') || conf_port=""
if [ -n "$conf_port" ] && [ "$conf_port" != "${PGPORT}" ]; then echo "PGPORT mismatch: env=${PGPORT} conf=${conf_port}" >&2; exit 3; fi
# write pg_hba.conf if missing (dev-only: trust)
if [ ! -f "$CONF_DIR/pg_hba.conf" ]; then
  sudo bash -lc "cat > '$CONF_DIR/pg_hba.conf' <<EOF
local   all             all                                     trust
host    all             all             127.0.0.1/32            trust
host    all             all             ::1/128                 trust
EOF"
fi
sudo chown -R postgres:postgres "$CONF_DIR"
# runner: execute SQL template as postgres (uses trust auth)
cat > "$SCRIPTS_DIR/run_create_user_db.sh" <<'BASH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE:-/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/dt3_bootcamp_database/PostgreSQLDatabase}"
SCRIPTS_DIR="$WORKSPACE/scripts"
: ${PGUSER:=devuser}; : ${PGDATABASE:=devdb}; : ${PGPASSWORD:=devpass}; : ${PGPORT:=5432}
sudo -u postgres psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -h 127.0.0.1 -p "$PGPORT" -U postgres -f "$SCRIPTS_DIR/create_dev_user_db.sql" -v app_user="$PGUSER" -v app_pass="$PGPASSWORD" -v app_db="$PGDATABASE"
BASH
chmod 750 "$SCRIPTS_DIR/run_create_user_db.sh"
sudo chown postgres:postgres "$SCRIPTS_DIR/run_create_user_db.sh"

steps.name: start - start persistent Postgres instance using workspace data and configs
steps.description: Start Postgres as postgres user pointed at the workspace data dir and generated conf files; intended for agents that want a long-running dev DB. Uses the persisted PGPORT and validates readiness. Does not stop system postgres. Documents intended use.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE:-/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/dt3_bootcamp_database/PostgreSQLDatabase}"
DATA_DIR="$WORKSPACE/data"; CONF_DIR="$WORKSPACE/conf"
[ -f /etc/profile.d/pg_dev_env.sh ] && source /etc/profile.d/pg_dev_env.sh || true
: ${PGPORT:=5432}
sudo -u postgres pg_ctl -D "$DATA_DIR" -o "-c config_file=$CONF_DIR/postgresql.conf -c hba_file=$CONF_DIR/pg_hba.conf" -w start
# readiness
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do sudo -u postgres pg_isready -p "$PGPORT" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break || sleep 1; if [ "$i" -eq 5 ]; then echo "start: postgres not ready" >&2; exit 4; fi; done
echo "postgres started (data=$DATA_DIR port=${PGPORT})"

steps.summary: Created a set of validation helper scripts under .init to perform the final validation step: start the workspace Postgres instance briefly, confirm readiness, run healthcheck, run pg_restore --list if a dump exists, then stop the server and emit OK. Scripts are idempotent, non-interactive, use the authoritative workspace path, and adhere to strict error handling. No architect escalation required.
steps.qa_summary: Engineer provided clear evidence that the validation step was implemented: helper scripts (start, stop, test, build, validation) were created to start the workspace Postgres instance briefly, confirm readiness, run healthcheck, run pg_restore --list if a dump exists, then stop the server and emit OK. Scripts are idempotent, non-interactive, use the authoritative workspace path fallback, and include strict error handling. No critical errors or escalations were reported.

reasoning: Keep setup minimal and non-invasive while addressing analyst feedback. Key decisions: avoid unreliable workspace PGPASSWORD wrapper and instead rely on dev-only trust auth for administrative operations executed as the postgres Unix user (sudo -u postgres psql). Persist PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPORT to /etc/profile.d but do not persist PGPASSWORD; set /etc/profile.d to mode 644 so shells can source it. Ensure all scripts accept an externally injected WORKSPACE via WORKSPACE environment variable fallback to the authoritative workspace path (no hardcoded multiple literals). Make postgresql.conf generation consume the same PGPORT available in the environment by reading /etc/profile.d (or env) at runtime and validate that port matches persisted value. Replace the healthcheck to use postgres superuser / pg_isready to avoid false negatives before app user creation. Remove silent error swallowing (no '|| true'). Add an explicit 'start' script for persistent dev runs. Scripts are concise but maintain idempotency and strict error handling.

change_logs.message: Refined initial plan to address analyst feedback: modified env-001 to safely persist env vars and detect/persist an available port (fixes CRITICAL). Fixed heredoc and variable expansion in config-001; created idempotent SQL creation using psql -v (fixes HIGH). Removed executable bit from SQL and unified filename (scaffold-001 and config-001 change). Hardened /etc/profile.d file permissions and added a workspace-scoped wrapper to avoid exposing PGPASSWORD globally (addresses MEDIUM). Updated test-001 and validation-001 to detect running system postgres, use alternate port when needed, verify server readiness with retry loop, and confirm dump/restore. These changes address the CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM issues from the analyst feedback.

Refinements to address analyst CRITICAL/HIGH issues: env-001 updated to persist PGPORT/PGDATABASE/PGUSER with mode 644 and removed the unreliable pg_pass_wrapper; scripts now rely on sudo -u postgres + trust auth for admin psql invocations. scaffold-001 healthcheck changed to use pg_isready/psql -U postgres to avoid app-user false negatives. All scripts now derive WORKSPACE from WORKSPACE env or fallback to the authoritative path (fixes hardcoded paths). config-001 changed to read persisted PGPORT (from environment or /etc/profile.d) and validate that postgresql.conf port matches persisted PGPORT. test-001 removed '|| true' and now runs run_create_user_db.sh as sudo -u postgres (no env propagation needed). Added start-001 to provide a documented persistent start path. These changes address the feedback about PGPASSWORD handling, healthcheck user mismatch, workspace hardcoding, port consistency, /etc/profile.d permissions, error swallowing, and missing start step.

qa_summary: The plan covers all required categories (environment, scaffolding, configuration/build, start, test, validation) and provides idempotent, non-interactive shell scripts that use preinstalled PostgreSQL tools. There are no CRITICAL gaps that would make the plan unusable. I recommend a small set of pragmatic fixes and hardening tweaks (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) to improve robustness, portability, and safety during automated runs.
qa_issues: Step 'env-001': uses `ss` to detect port 5432 availability; `ss` may not be present in constrained images (though likely present on Ubuntu) and there's no fallback. The port-selection logic does not persist the chosen port atomically if race conditions occur.

Step 'env-001': /etc/profile.d/pg_dev_env.sh is world-readable (644) per design; that permits non-root shells to read PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPORT. The plan intentionally avoids persisting PGPASSWORD, but callers must still be aware that some tools may expect PGPASSWORD to be set (documented but not automated).

Step 'scaffold-001': The SQL template uses psql client substitution variable syntax inside a DO $$ ... $$ block (uses :'app_user', :'app_pass', :'app_db'). While psql variable substitution will replace occurrence before sending SQL to server, complex quoting inside DO blocks may produce unexpected quoting/escaping results depending on inputs. This could fail for identifier vs literal substitution if values contain unusual characters.

Step 'config-001': initdb is executed only when DATA_DIR/PG_VERSION is absent, but if an existing system postgres is using shared configuration directories or if DATA_DIR already contains partial files the script may not detect a mismatched cluster version. There is no explicit check of initdb version compatibility.

Step 'config-001' and 'start-001'/'test-001'/'validation-001': The generated postgresql.conf and pg_hba.conf are written into WORKSPACE/conf, and pg_ctl is started pointing to the DATA_DIR with explicit config_file and hba_file. This is acceptable, but there is potential for conflict if the system-installed Postgres service is running and already bound to the chosen port; the plan selects an alternate port only in env-001 but doesn't validate again before starting the custom server.

Step 'scaffold-001' & 'config-001': healthcheck scripts call sudo -u postgres psql without setting PGHOST/PGPORT explicitly in all invocations (some calls rely on environment). Some invocations use 127.0.0.1 while others may rely on PGPORT from /etc/profile.d - this inconsistent usage could cause false negatives if env isn't sourced.

Step 'test-001' & 'validation-001': timeouts during readiness loops are short (5 iterations with 1s sleeps) which may be insufficient on busy or resource-constrained environments. There is inconsistent cleanup on failure (some places attempt stop || true, others exit leaving server running).

General script-size guidance: several scripts exceed the 'target 5-15 lines' guidance. While they are concise and structured, consider minor consolidation to meet the guideline if line-count is a hard requirement.

Step metadata: 'config-001' uses script_name 'build' and category 'configuration' — this is valid per provided allowed names, but category vs script_name mismatch might confuse some orchestrators expecting 'configuration' category to use a specific script_name. Not a correctness bug, but noteable.

qa_recommendations.description: Step 'env-001': Add a fallback for port detection if `ss` is not available (e.g., check `ss || netstat -tlnp || lsof -i :5432`) and ensure atomic persistence of the chosen port: after selecting an ephemeral port, validate that nothing bound it between selection and writing /etc/profile.d, or choose port at start-time if pg_ctl/start will check. Update the script to retry a small number of times if race is detected.

Step 'scaffold-001' and 'config-001': Replace or harden the psql variable substitution usage inside the DO $$ block. Two safer approaches: (a) generate plain SQL statements using the client-side psql substitution but avoid DO blocks (use CREATE ROLE ... IF NOT EXISTS style with safe quoting) or (b) use a small POSIX-safe here-doc that passes values via `psql -c "..."` constructed in the runner script where quoting is controlled. Modify 'run_create_user_db.sh' to build a safe SQL payload or use SQL functions that accept literal parameters to avoid quoting errors.

Step 'config-001': After initdb, check the cluster PG_VERSION and compare against the installed postgres major version to detect incompatibility. Fail fast with an explicit message when DATA_DIR contains an incompatible cluster rather than proceeding silently.

Step 'start-001', 'test-001', 'validation-001': Before starting the workspace Postgres, re-check that the configured PGPORT is available (race may have occurred since env persistence). If port is taken, either pick another ephemeral port and update the runtime postgresql.conf before starting, or exit with a clear error. Also make readiness loops a bit more tolerant (e.g., up to 10 attempts with 1s sleep) and ensure consistent cleanup on failure (always attempt pg_ctl -w stop).

Step 'scaffold-001' and healthcheck scripts: Make environment sourcing consistent. Healthcheck and runner scripts should explicitly source /etc/profile.d/pg_dev_env.sh (or read PGPORT/PGHOST from defaults passed as flags) so they don't rely on the agent's shell environment. Also include explicit -h 127.0.0.1 and -p "$PGPORT" on all psql/pg_isready invocations to avoid ambiguity.

Step 'env-001': Add a short comment in the summary to document the deliberate decision not to persist PGPASSWORD and how automated agents should supply credentials for application-level tests (e.g., inject via environment for the process, use .pgpass in workspace for automated tests if necessary).

Step 'scaffold-001' and 'config-001': Consider making the created SQL template and runner more explicit about allowed characters in usernames/passwords (or sanitize/validate in the runner) to avoid injection or quoting errors in automated non-interactive runs.

General: Consider small consolidation to reduce script line counts if you need to hit the 5-15 line target strictly—e.g., combine simple file writes and chown operations into single sudo bash -lc grouped heredocs, but keep readability and error handling intact.

Metadata note: Step 'config-001' uses script_name 'build' while category is 'configuration'. This is allowed, but if orchestration tooling expects 'configuration' to map to a specific script_name, either rename the script_name to 'build' (kept) or document the mapping. No functional change required.
